According to reports, Apple recorded its first annual sales revenue exceeding US$10 billion (approximately HK$78 billion) in India in the previous fiscal year.

In a country where the average annual income per capita is less than US$3,000 (approximately HK$23,400), this achievement is all the more remarkable—especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the United States...

For many years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. However, with the rapid economic development of the country in recent years, coupled with Apple finally being able to open Apple Stores there, the situation has changed dramatically.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given India's lower per capita income and the fact that iPhones are manufactured locally, one might expect prices to be significantly lower than in the United States. In reality, however, high taxes make Apple products more expensive in India than in the US.

Apple has attempted to offset this issue somewhat by partnering with banks to offer credit card cashback.

Currently, about a quarter of iPhones are manufactured in India, but most are sold to the US market. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements with the aim of avoiding US tariffs imposed on products imported from China.
